faq: How much ad budget should I plan?

Enough to collect meaningful data, which depends on your price and category. We suggest a starting daily budget from your margin, and you can lower, pause or raise it any time. Amazon bills you directly.
Can you promise a target ACoS?
No. We set targets and work toward them, but results depend on your listing, price, reviews and competition. We show the actual figures and explain them honestly.
How is this different from PPC management?
This is a fixed set-up with one or two review rounds. PPC management is a deeper keyword and bid project with more tuning during the sprint. Choose by how much help you want.
Do you need my ad account?
Yes, access through Seller Central or Amazon Ads user permissions. We manage campaigns and view reports, while billing and login details stay with you.

desc:
Amazon Sponsored Products ads setup puts your listings in front of shoppers who are already searching. Ecom Swift LLC chooses the products to advertise, builds auto and manual campaigns, sets budgets from your margins, adds negative keywords and reports back in plain words.

## What are Amazon Sponsored Products ads?

Sponsored Products are pay-per-click ads for individual listings. They appear in search results and on product pages, and you pay when a shopper clicks, not when the ad is shown. Each ad points to a product you already sell, so the quality of the listing behind it matters as much as the campaign itself.

## Why a first campaign needs planning

New sellers often switch on automatic ads with a default budget and wait. The result is usually spend on broad search terms that never buy, and no clear way to tell what worked. Ads also lift the cost of every sale, so a campaign that ignores your margin can sell products at a loss.

A planned start reverses that. You decide which product to advertise first, what each click is worth to you, and how much you are willing to spend before you review the data. That gives the campaign a clear limit and a clear question to answer.

## How ads affect visibility and sales

Amazon shows ads to shoppers whose search matches a keyword or a product. A listing with no reviews or sales history can be hard to find in organic results, and an ad gives it a place on the first page while that history builds. Clicks and orders from ads also tell Amazon which searches your product is relevant for.

Auto campaigns let Amazon match your listing to searches, and they reveal the terms shoppers really use. Manual campaigns let you choose keywords and bids with more control. Used together, the first finds ideas and the second puts money behind the ones that work. Results depend on price, reviews, stock, images and competition, so we do not promise a return or a target cost of sales.

## What a well-built Sponsored Products setup includes

- A shortlist of products worth advertising, based on margin, stock and listing quality.
- An auto campaign with a daily budget that fits your spend limit.
- Manual campaigns grouped by match type and product.
- Starting bids calculated from your selling price and costs.
- Negative keywords that block irrelevant searches from the first day.
- Clear campaign names so reports are easy to read.
- Sponsored Brands campaigns where your brand is eligible.
- A review of search term reports after the first few days of data.
- A written summary with the next adjustments.

## How we run the work

We begin with your product list, prices, costs and the monthly amount you plan to spend. From these we work out what a click can cost before an order loses money. We then build the campaigns inside your own advertising console and add the first negative keywords.

After the campaigns have gathered some data, we read the search term report, pause terms that waste budget, raise bids on terms that convert, and move good terms into manual campaigns. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of products, whether manual campaigns and Sponsored Brands are included, and how many review rounds you get. Ad spend goes directly from your account to Amazon.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Advertise products with clear images, a healthy margin and stock on hand.
- Set a daily budget you are comfortable losing while you learn.
- Review search terms before raising any bid.
- Give campaigns a few days of data before judging them.
- Keep notes on every change so results can be traced.

**Avoid:**
- Advertising a listing that has poor images or a weak title.
- Bidding on competitor brand names.
- Changing bids and budgets every day.
- Switching ads on for products that may run out of stock.
- Copying settings from another seller without checking your margin.

## Who this is for

This service suits a new seller whose listings are live but invisible and who needs a safe first campaign. It also suits an owner who tried ads once, saw money spent with little to show, and wants a clean structure. A brand with a few strong products can use it to add manual targeting on top of an existing auto campaign.

## What we need from you

Please send your list of products, your cost and price for each, your monthly spend limit and any keywords you already know work. You invite us as a user in your Seller Central and advertising console with the permissions needed to build and edit campaigns. We never ask for your password, and we do not move your money.
